name: Where Fear and Weapons Meet
label: Revelation
lede: South Florida kids from Morning Again and Poison the Well made fifteen songs in twenty-one minutes for Revelation, with half of the local scene yelling along in the back.

eras.title: Out of Morning Again
eras.text: When Morning Again broke up, John Wylie and drummer Jason Lederman started something faster and simpler: fun, catchy hardcore without the metal that was taking over Florida. Revelation signed them off one five-song record.

years.h: Where Fear and Weapons Meet form in South Florida
years.p: Guitarist [[John Wylie|f587d49e-5157-4c8a-869c-c3f0f7b5b31c]] (ex-Culture, [[Morning Again|1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23]]) and drummer Jason Lederman team up with [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]]'s Ryan Primack on bass and singer Alex "Wall Street Justice" Flores.

years.src: Discogs · RevHQ · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Where Fear and Weapons Meet's debut 7" · Revelation REV 74
years.p: Five songs cut at Studio 13 in Deerfield Beach. Revelation sold it as traditional, fun, catchy hardcore; the first press included 220 on clear vinyl.
years.xp:
The back cover has a misprint: the fourth song is listed as Other Face, the same as the opener, instead of Above Water. The labels and lyric sheet get it right. And Never and Meant to Be are listed as two tracks but play as one song.

Jeff Caudill of [[Gameface|c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27]] did the layout.

eras.title: Fifteen songs, twenty-one minutes
eras.text: The one full-length is the record people still mean when they bring this band up. Then the singer and bassist left, and the band kept going on smaller labels with a different sound.

years.p: Recorded in April 1999 at Studio 13 in Deerfield Beach: fifteen songs in about 21 minutes. Guest backing vocals include Chad from [[Shai Hulud|2aaa7913-72ae-469b-9fdb-4c79cd70ed2e]] and Steve from [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]].
years.xp:
The credits use stage names: Alex Wall Street Justice on vocals, John Pain on guitar, Ryan Powers on bass, Jason Deucifer on drums. The gang vocals read like a roll call of the late-'90s South Florida scene.

Revelation's first press included 222 on orange vinyl.

years.h: Alex Flores and Ryan Primack leave; Larry Scott takes the mic
years.p: After The Weapon, singer Alex Flores and bassist Ryan Primack leave. Larry Scott, co-owner of Think Fast! Records, sings and Chad Kishick plays bass.
years.xp: One longtime fan blog's verdict: the band lost a bit of its tightness and speed with the new lineup.

years.h: Split with Comin' Correct on Temperance Records
years.p: Where Fear and Weapons Meet share a record with Comin' Correct on Temperance.
Where Fear and Weapons Meet's first release after leaving Revelation, on Triple Crown.

eras.title: The original voice comes back
eras.text: A second guitar from Until the End, the first singer back at the mic, and one last record on Eulogy before the band quietly stopped.

years.h: Chip Walbert joins on second guitar
years.p: [[Chip Walbert|a5cf7b12-0fdf-432c-bec4-3e192f473dd8]] of [[Until the End|b366ca2e-a474-48b8-866c-e4d10fb1c1dc]] plays second guitar alongside John Wylie.
Alex Flores returns on vocals for Where Fear and Weapons Meet's last release, on Eulogy with Think Fast!.

years.h: Where Fear and Weapons Meet break up
years.p: Where Fear and Weapons Meet stop. Members' other bands over the years include Against All Authority, Poison the Well, Shai Hulud, Morning Again and Until the End.

eras.title: Bringin' it back for the kids
eras.text: Florida's reunion festival brought the band back for one weekend with a mix of old members and later ones.

years.cap: Where Fear and Weapons Meet · via Discogs
years.h: Where Fear and Weapons Meet reunite in Pompano Beach
years.p: Announced in June, the reunion at Bringin' It Back for the Kids Fest 2 has original members plus Larry Scott on vocals, Chip Walbert and Chad Kishick. Trapped Under Ice, the Mongoloids and Backtrack share the bill.
